meta.title: ElectroMap: Stories of the World
meta.description: An interactive map installation for UWC Day's «Share Peace Story» workshop — practising active curiosity toward places far from us, starting from the stories that come from there.
meta.summary: It was UWC Day, theme «Share Peace Story». Jun and I made this together.

blocks.text: The starting point was a Yixi talk recommended by my friend Liang Yue, in which the artist Liang Zi referenced «COLORS: A Magazine About the Rest of the World». Liang Zi said: every story happening in the world has to do with you and me.
It was UWC Day; the theme was «Share Peace Story». So Jun and I made this.

blocks.text: I thought — a map can be a vehicle for that too. To draw people from everywhere into curiosity about places far from them.

items: Press the button beside a region you're curious about — a red dot is added, and the LED for that region on the map warms in colour.
On the right, a screen pops up a small story-card entry for that region; you can search the rest online.
Different from how media renders the world with intent — this is an active curiosity, a search for more real people and stories.
The warmer/cooler colour of each region's light reflects how many people are paying attention there. A small invitation to look at places that get overlooked.

blocks.text: I'd hoped people from different hometowns would share their own stories. The actual response wasn't large. So besides what I knew and the few entries people sent in, ChatGPT was used to find stories from around the world that fit the theme.
Engagement during the display was higher than I expected. Sharing one note we received —
At this point, this activity was already enough for me :3

I gave the participants too much to do — they only got the Micro:bit programming part and didn't get to assemble onto the map together. Next workshop, I have to weigh real take-home complexity carefully, and let people enjoy the making.

Some members didn't engage much; I didn't push, since some might just want to relax. Next time I want to be more aware of these members — to tell whether they're choosing not to join or wanting to but unable to follow. If it's the latter, I won't ignore it — I'll design more carefully so that people of different temperaments and minds each have a comfortable place. Of course I know it can't be perfect; what matters is that I care and think about it seriously, never ignore it.

items: Thank you Jun for making this with me — he built the casing and map; I did the Micro:bit programming and assembly.
Thank you Jun, Pranjal, Shruti for helping during the workshop, and every participant.
Thank you to everyone who interacted with the finished map during the display.
